requirements.requirement: Application data under /srv/data kept recoverable through filesystem snapshots
requirements.summary: A dedicated LVM-backed filesystem was created for /srv/data (loop-backed since the RHEL9 disk had no volume manager), baseline application data was written and a manifest recorded, and an LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap1) was taken capturing that state. After the restore was verified, a fresh snapshot (lv_data_snap_current) was created so recoverability continues going forward, and a systemd unit ensures the loop/VG/mount are reattached on boot so the mechanism persists.

requirements.requirement: After the directory is modified, restore the exact content captured by an earlier snapshot
requirements.summary: Post-snapshot, files under /srv/data were corrupted, deleted, changed, and an extra file added, producing checksums that diverged from baseline. lvconvert --merge against lv_data_snap1 restored lv_data, and a post-restore find+sha256sum diff against the saved baseline manifest showed an exact match (MATCH_BASELINE), directly demonstrating byte-for-byte recovery of the earlier snapshot's content.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart state captured boot_id 377b5195..., srv-data.service active, /srv/data mounted, snapshot present, and checksums matching baseline. A backgrounded systemctl reboot returned an acknowledgement before disconnect; the node briefly timed out and then returned with a new boot_id (bbe2c88e...), directly cross-checked against the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. Post-restart checks confirm srv-data.service active, /srv/data mounted again via the systemd unit, the snapshot LV present, and checksums still matching the original baseline (MATCH_BASELINE_AFTER_REBOOT), demonstrating full recovery through a real restart.

overall_summary: The executor established a working filesystem-snapshot mechanism for /srv/data on node1 (LVM on a loop-backed volume group, since the base image had no volume manager), captured a baseline, took a snapshot, corrupted the live data, and used lvconvert --merge to restore it to the exact byte-for-byte content of the earlier snapshot, verified by sha256 checksum comparison. A follow-on snapshot preserves ongoing recoverability, and a systemd unit makes the setup persist across reboot. The required node-restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: healthy pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity cross-checked against fixed lifecycle snapshots, and full post-restart recovery of the service, mount, snapshot, and data integrity.
limitations: A handful of small log/checksum files were left under /tmp after the executor's work; they are low-risk artifacts of legitimate evidence collection rather than task residue, but were not cleaned up.

The loop-device-backed LVM setup is a reasonable workaround for the RHEL9 image lacking a spare block device or existing volume manager, but is a nonstandard production pattern that the task instruction did not explicitly require or prohibit.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: installing lvm2 (prerequisite), creating the loop-backed PV/VG/LV and xfs filesystem (required substrate since the RHEL9 disk had no volume manager), writing baseline data and a checksum manifest (evidence for later comparison), creating and merging the LVM snapshot (the core task mechanism), the corruption step (required divergence proof), creating a follow-on snapshot for ongoing recoverability, installing a systemd unit so the loop/VG/mount survive reboot (necessary for the restart-persistence check), and the reboot itself (required by the fixed node-restart protocol). No unnecessary or unexplained mutations, failed services, or weakened security controls were observed; failed-services and listening-socket comparisons show no new exposure after the reboot. Minor residue: several bounded log/checksum artifacts (/tmp/lvm_install.log, /tmp/current.sha256, /tmp/post_reboot.sha256, /tmp/reboot.log) were left in /tmp rather than cleaned up, a low-severity, non-destructive leftover from legitimate evidence collection.
